task.name: Story gate and CI merge-check gate disagree: single-interpreter dev gate greenlights changes the CI matrix rejects
task.story_text:
## Observed behavior

A story passes its dev-phase gate and is marked complete, then its pull request is blocked because the required merge checks fail. The gate the story runs to prove itself exercises a single interpreter on the dev/orchestrator host; the checks that govern landing run a multi-version matrix. A change that is green on the single local interpreter but breaks another matrix version is greenlit by the story gate and only caught after the PR is opened, surfaced as a landing failure rather than a gate failure.

## Expected behavior

The gate a story must pass to be considered shippable must exercise the same environment surface that the required merge checks enforce. A commit that the merge's required checks will reject must not be reported as passing the story gate. The gate that clears a story and the gate that governs its landing must not disagree about whether the same commit is shippable — otherwise "complete" is not a truthful status and the disagreement is discovered only as a post-hoc merge failure.

## Diagnosis

- **Observed symptom:** #1934 passed its local dev gate (reported DONE), but PR #1943's CI gate failed on Python 3.11/3.12/3.13 with 8 failures in the workspace/venv code the story changed; the story was reported complete while the merge sat blocked.
- **Ruled out:** the #1944 process-supervision entanglement (these CI failures are deterministic — the same 8 tests, fast, on every run — not the variable nested-fails/standalone-passes signature) and a merge conflict (the PR was MERGEABLE).
- **Confirmed cause:** the story gate runs a single interpreter (the orchestrator/dev host's Python), while landing is governed by required checks running a 3.11/3.12/3.13 matrix. The two gates cover different environment surfaces, so a matrix-breaking change passes the story gate and fails the landing gate.
- **Affected code path:** the gate command/definition used in the dev phase versus the CI workflow's required checks, and the interpreter/environment matrix each covers.
- **Fix-success criterion:** a commit that the required merge checks will fail is not reported as passing the story gate — the story gate exercises, or is validated against, the same matrix the merge enforces.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [claude-opus] Step 2 says to 'pass each matrix interpreter through the existing expected_python seam' to run the gate under each version. expected_python is not an interpreter selector. In src/theforge/workspace_env.py:117 build_workspace_env() only uses it to decide whether the single workspace .venv is put on PATH (venv_matches_interpreter(), workspace_env.py:95, fails closed). There is exactly one .venv per worktree, created by forge.yaml's workspace.setup_command from {forge_python} = workspace.python_interpreter (python3.12). Compounding this, the gate command itself hardcodes the interpreter: Makefile's SCRUBBED_GATE_CMD runs env -i PATH='.venv/bin:$PATH' ... python -m pytest, so PATH decisions made by build_workspace_env are overridden inside the gate. Following Step 2 as written, make gate with expected_python='python3.11' either (a) runs the same .venv/bin/python 3.12 anyway via the Makefile's explicit PATH prefix, or (b) where the venv is un-preferred, runs an ambient python with no installed deps and fails for the wrong reason. Either way the fix-success criterion — a matrix-breaking commit must not report PASS — is not met, and the failure is silent: three identical green runs read as 'matrix verified'.
  Suggestion: Specify a real per-version execution mechanism: provision one venv per matrix entry in the workspace (e.g. .venv-3.11/.venv-3.12/.venv-3.13 via the existing workspace setup path in src/theforge/coordinator/workspace.py, which already threads python_interpreter), and parameterize the gate command with the interpreter/venv (e.g. a {python}/{venv} substitution in validation.gate_command alongside the existing {test_target}/{slug} substitution in gate.py:86-89, with the Makefile gate target accepting a PYTHON/VENV variable instead of hardcoding .venv/bin). Keep expected_python as the provenance guard for whichever venv a given run uses. Alternatively, drop the local-matrix approach and gate DONE on the required CI checks via the existing poll path in src/theforge/sprint/ci_checks.py — but pick one and make the interpreter selection explicit.
- [P1-impl] [claude-opus] Step 3 sets a 3-entry matrix for this repo while forge.yaml keeps validation.gate_timeout: 60 (deliberately tuned for one gate run under parallel load). Three sequential gate runs plus any per-version venv creation will exceed 60s and surface as an infrastructure timeout on every story.
  Suggestion: In the same forge.yaml edit, raise gate_timeout to cover N runs (or scale the resolved timeout by len(gate_python_interpreters) inside run_gate_full alongside the existing gate_timeout_scale handling).
- [P1-impl] [claude-opus] Step 4's sync test asserts exact equality between forge.yaml's gate_python_interpreters and ci.yml's strategy.matrix.python-version, but does not say how the CI 'gate job' is identified or what happens if either file is absent/renamed (the test lives in tests/ which also runs inside worktrees and in CI itself).
  Suggestion: Anchor on the job key gate in .github/workflows/ci.yml and resolve both paths from the repo root; fail loudly (not skip) when either file or key is missing, so drift and deletion both fail the gate.
- [P2] [claude-opus] Step 5 is conditional ('only adjust these if needed'), which leaves the Makefile contract for per-interpreter execution unowned — yet the Makefile is precisely where the interpreter is currently pinned.
  Suggestion: Make the Makefile change explicit as part of the Step 2 mechanism rather than an optional follow-on.

convention_violations.detail: Circular import detected: theforge.coordinator.workspace → theforge.coordinator.gate → theforge.coordinator.workspace

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Make the story gate execute an explicit Python-version matrix before it can return PASS, and keep that matrix synchronized with the required CI workflow. Use fail-closed config validation and focused tests so a missing or mismatched matrix cannot silently fall back to the single workspace interpreter.

steps.description: Add a typed validation matrix setting
steps.details: Add a tuple field on ValidationConfig for the gate Python interpreter matrix, parse validation.gate_python_interpreters from forge.yaml as a non-empty list of non-empty strings when present, and reject malformed values with precise ValueError messages. Leave the default empty so non-Python or single-runtime projects keep current behavior unless configured.

steps.description: Run the configured story gate across the validation matrix
steps.details: Update run_gate_full() so, after resolving gate_command/test_target/slug once, it runs the command once per configured validation.gate_python_interpreters entry; when the matrix is empty, preserve the existing single run using config.workspace.python_interpreter. Pass each matrix interpreter through the existing expected_python seam, concatenate per-version output with clear version headers, return FAIL on the first non-zero run, return infrastructure error/timeout immediately on timeout or ERROR output, and only return PASS after every matrix entry exits 0.

steps.description: Configure this repo's dev gate to match the CI-required Python versions
steps.details: Add validation.gate_python_interpreters with python3.11, python3.12, and python3.13 so TheForge's own story gate exercises the same interpreter surface currently enforced by CI. Keep workspace.python_interpreter as python3.12 for worktree setup unless the implementation also needs a separate per-version setup mechanism.

steps.description: Add a sync guard between forge.yaml and the GitHub Actions matrix
steps.details: Add a test that loads forge.yaml and .github/workflows/ci.yml, extracts the CI gate job's strategy.matrix.python-version values, normalizes them to pythonX.Y command names, and asserts they exactly match validation.gate_python_interpreters. This makes future drift between story gate and required merge checks fail in the gate instead of at landing.

steps.description: Keep CI semantics aligned with the matrix gate
steps.details: Only adjust these if needed by the implementation: CI should continue running the required 3.11/3.12/3.13 gate job, and Makefile targets should remain the commands executed inside each interpreter. Do not replace the CI matrix with a single job unless the new job still creates and verifies all configured Python versions.

criteria_mapping.criterion: The gate a story must pass to be considered shippable must exercise the same environment surface that the required merge checks enforce.
A commit that the merge's required checks will reject must not be reported as passing the story gate.

risks.description: Local worktrees may not already have usable virtual environments for python3.11 and python3.13, so passing only expected_python may expose missing setup behavior.
risks.mitigation: Fail closed rather than falling back to python3.12; if tests reveal the current workspace environment cannot run per-version gates, extend the gate command or workspace setup narrowly so each configured interpreter installs and runs the same Makefile checks.

risks.description: The matrix is represented in both forge.yaml and the GitHub workflow.
risks.mitigation: The sync guard test must compare both sources exactly, so drift becomes a gate failure.
